quotes.text: The First Keeper turned away, vowing never to cast offerings again.
Greed whispered in his ear: "Why return any? The gift was freely given. The river has already done its work."
in a valley of takers, even measured trust is foolishness.
Each of you believed you were wise to protect yourself. Each of you was right to distrust the others.
The myths are armor made of words, protecting us from the nakedness of our own cowardice.
They saw themselves send nothing, round after round.
The valley stayed frozen. The myths stayed beautiful. Nothing moved.
Wisdom without courage is just elaborate knowledge of chains.
You know that someone must move first.
"If you know all this, why do you still write? Why not just... stop?"
Each betrayal begat another. Each defection was justified by the last.
sometimes it whispered false numbers to those who counted too carefully

note: River of Abundance turns to collective betrayal and frozen villages; narrators justify distrust then confess cowardice; no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: send the full treasure with courage, and return an equitable share with unyielding honor.
to send the complete measure with courage, and to return an equitable share with unwavering virtue.
he returned half the blossoming light—seven and a half celestial blooms—back across the divide
They understood that the mists were transient illusions, but the pact of mutual honor was eternal.

note: Sower/Keeper template every round: cast all five, return 8 then exactly half, ignore mists. No sanction.
